sentences.text: This extinct penguin genus belongs to the family Spheniscidae, which includes modern penguins.
Smaller bones found in the genus have been assigned to Pseudaptenodytes minor, though it is uncertain if they represent a distinct species or just younger individuals.
The extinct penguin genus Pseudaptenodytes was described by Simpson in 1970.
The type species of the genus is Pseudaptenodytes macraei, while Pseudaptenodytes minor is a disputed species. The genus Pseudaptenodytes contains the type species Pseudaptenodytes macraei.

Fossils of Pseudaptenodytes were found in Victoria, Australia, in deposits dating to the Late Miocene or Early Pliocene. The animal lived between 7.246 and 5.333 million years ago during the Messinian stage.
